title: Europe has since become Americanized and polluted
summary: He describes changes in Switzerland and Holland since 1968: traffic, parking, polluted lake and smog.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now in trying to go from here to there, they are picking up the same tempo pace that we are talking about here.
That's right. They are. In business they have become just as hard as American business. I've noticed that. I mean, they obviously think that it's...
The ball is bouncing the other way, there's no doubt. When you go there and you see drug stores... In Paris you see skyscrapers and things going on. That's the last bastion of, you know, that...

Well, look, it has to do with what you said. If this country's population is 330 million (sic) and it's like the top dog, it's going to influence all the countries that have depended on it. That stands to reason.
They become involved...have to be involved.
Yeah. I mean, they adopt American ways of business and everything.
I remember when I went to Switzerland back in '68, I was amazed! I have pictures from the Bauhofplatz(?)

when it was practically deserted. It was so nice and tranquil. Now, the (?) Grill is gone, and they're digging underneath for parking space. And in Holland, where it was a pleasure and an achievement to bicycle from Rotterdam to Amsterdam, because it's flat... I mean, you can shoot a bullet and it runs a mile! Now, there's no such thing of people doing that. They have highways going PSHWOO, full of people, cars are racing, you know...

It's different. It's unbelievable. I once went to see Johnny Simmens. I remember when Johnny Simmens' house was lost in the beauty of these trees and bushes. Now you can't get to his house where the cars park double-parked!
The lake... I remember I used to swim in the lake. I almost drowned there, but I came out of it...

Now it's polluted. You see (?). It's unbelievable. I wouldn't even put my foot in the lake now. And then, of course, there's no escape, because as you zero into Zurich and suddenly you see the Alps... The mountains aren't immune from that. Smog. As high as the mountains are, they're involved, because the planes(?) are up there dropping this smog. So you could hardly see the city for the smog.
